workflows.title: WF6 Vehicle API abuse
workflows.description: Partner or app key enumerating VINs or trying remote commands on customer cars.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead F.  
**You need:** the API key id.  
**Goal:** decide whether a key is being abused and whether any customer vehicle data was exposed.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

steps.title: Is this key behaving differently from the others?

evidence.title: Error rate by key
evidence.expr: sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | status >= 400 [$__interval])) / sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json [$__interval]))

card.look: error rate per key over time.
card.bad: one key's error rate far above the others (normal is about 2%).
card.if_clean: this key looks like every other key. Close the lead.

steps.title: Where are the requests coming from?

evidence.title: Sources getting errors on this key
evidence.expr: topk(25, sum by (src_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | status >= 400 [$__range])))

evidence.title: All sources for this key, last 15 minutes

card.bad: an address outside the partner's registered egress range (`198.18.0.0/15` in this demo) sending most of the errors.
card.if_bad: that address is the abuser. Block it at the gateway and go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: all traffic is from the partner's range. Their system may be broken, not compromised. Call the partner.

evidence.title: Endpoints and outcomes
evidence.expr: sum by (method, endpoint, status) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" [$__range]))

card.look: endpoints and outcomes for this key.
card.bad: a wall of 404s on `/vehicles/{vin}/...` (guessing VINs), or any `/remote/` command (unlock, start).
card.if_bad: remote command attempts escalate to the vehicle security team right away.

steps.title: Did they get any customer data?

evidence.title: What was returned
evidence.expr: sum by (endpoint, src_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | status=200 | src_ip!~"198[.]18[.].*" [$__range]))

card.look: successful responses to addresses outside the partner range.
card.bad: any 200. Each one is a real vehicle's status or location returned to the abuser.
card.if_bad: this is a privacy incident. Privacy and legal need the count and the time range.
card.if_clean: zero successes. Enumeration failed. Still revoke the key.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Abuse** if Step 1 is red and Step 2 shows an unregistered source.

**Do these now:**
1. Revoke the key and issue the partner a new one through their account manager.
2. Block the source address at the API gateway.
3. If Step 4 is above zero: open a privacy incident with the count of exposed vehicles.
4. If Step 3 shows remote commands: notify the vehicle security team.

**Then:** [[Case timeline for the source address]]

links.label: Case timeline for the source address

also.say: Customer vehicle data was returned. Open a privacy incident.

rule.close_if_false: Key behaves like the others. Close the lead.
